summary: Martin Peretz is an American former magazine publisher. He was also a Harvard University assistant professor. He was born on December 6, 1938. He bought The New Republic in 1974 for $380,000. In 1975 he fired its editor, Gilbert Harrison. Much of the staff was fired or quit. Peretz then edited the magazine until 1979. He later remained editor-in-chief as others edited. The magazine took liberal positions on economic and social issues. It took pro-Israel, hawkish stances on foreign affairs. Critics said he used it to attack opponents. In 1996 he co-founded TheStreet.com with Jim Cramer. He sold a two-thirds stake in the magazine in 2002. He sold the rest to CanWest in 2007. He bought it back with investors in 2009. In late 2010 he became editor emeritus. He no longer has any association with it. He supported the 2003 invasion of Iraq. Critics accused him of bigoted remarks about Arabs and Muslims. In 2010 he wrote that "Muslim life is cheap". He later apologised. Harvard then cancelled a speech he was to give.
